title: Trim
teaser: A weight-loss dashboard that turns your own Google Sheet into a weekly trend, with an optional AI coach.

sections.problem: I started a fitness program a few years ago with the aim of losing a few pounds. My personal aim was to track signals surrounding me that were influencing my goal positively or negatively. With a lot of data recorded, it made sense to me that some of what was missing was succinct summaries, conclusions against my signals, and a test to see if I could bring AI in to help synthesize all of the factors.
sections.build: A weekly-anchored dashboard that reads directly from one or more Google Sheets (public CSV export links, no API keys) and joins them by date into KPIs, a trend chart, and a Y/N daily-goal compliance card. Weeks are the atomic unit everywhere, not a rolling window, the current in-progress week shows a live count but withholds comparisons until it's actually complete. An optional Coach feature shells out locally to the Claude Code CLI to write a weekly verdict and recommendation, checking recent weeks of history before writing a new one.
sections.technical: A small Express server with no database, reading local JSON config and fetching Google Sheets CSV exports server-side. The dashboard itself has no built-in LLM calls; the one AI feature runs the Claude Code CLI headlessly on the user's own machine when they click Analyze Week, nothing is sent to a hosted API by the app. The public demo is a self-contained static build with fictional data, no server or Sheets connection needed to view it.
sections.learning: The agentic position on this app is pretty robust in terms of thinking through what all I should need to send in as context to be rationalized. Figuring out how I wanted to go about generating an agentic recommendation and then turn to feed a certain volume of them back in later periods to reinforce the ecosystem of activity was an exciting opportunity to dig further into.
sections.next: The coach currently has a specific personality. The next step I'd like to explore is creating multiple personas for the coach to meet a user at his/her preferred style and have the agentic piece speak more to the resolution that user might need for his/her own personal journey to be successful.
